inspections.text: The needle sits just past the first mark. Somebody has scratched a line in the brass where it used to rest.
inspections.title: The pressure dial

inspections.text: A tide table, a meeting on Thursday, and a drawing of a lost tortoise called Admiral. Last seen heading for the harbour.
inspections.title: Notices on the beacon

inspections.text: Locked. The keyhole is polished bright. Chalked on the step: BACK AT 4.
inspections.title: A small teal door

inspections.text: Up close, the root moves. Not much. About as much as someone asleep.
inspections.title: The beacon

inspections.text: Ten past nine. The bakery says five past. Nobody’s sure which to believe.
inspections.title: The guild hall clock

inspections.text: Parcels in brown paper, every one tied with the same knot. One is addressed in pencil to the lighthouse.
inspections.title: Post Office

inspections.text: Last collection 5.15. Someone has posted a pine cone. It’s still in the slot.
inspections.title: The post box

inspections.text: The beacon’s quarterly reading, a call for volunteers to repaint the railings, and a reward for a lost brass key.
inspections.title: Guild notices

inspections.text: The racks are half empty already. A card in the window: SECOND BATCH AT ELEVEN.
inspections.title: Morning Loaf

inspections.text: Oranges stacked into a careful pyramid. One is missing from the very top.
inspections.title: The greengrocer

inspections.text: Cloth, coats and repairs. A paper measuring tape hangs beside the glazed door.
inspections.title: Finch & Thread

inspections.text: Lemons by the crate and figs by the dozen. A chalkboard by the scales: PEACHES TOMORROW. Under it, smaller: PROBABLY.
inspections.title: The fruit market

inspections.text: The brass plate has been polished so often the H is half gone. Inside, a clerk counts the same stack of notes for the second time.
inspections.title: Haverlund Savings

inspections.text: Steam on the windows and a dish of sugar cubes on every table. A sign on the till: WE DO NOT SERVE GULLS.
inspections.title: The Harbour Cup

inspections.text: Today’s Haverlund Herald: TRAM No. 7 LATE AGAIN. The vendor has underlined AGAIN in pencil.
inspections.title: The news kiosk

inspections.text: Cold, and faintly of iron. The tin cup is chained on, and the chain is longer than it needs to be.
inspections.title: The drinking fountain

inspections.text: Buckets of sweet peas and stocks, and a jam jar of coins nobody is minding.
inspections.title: The flower stall

inspections.text: “FOUR PENCE. STOP. PLEASE COUNT IT. STOP. PLEASE COUNT IT AGAIN. STOP.”
inspections.title: Tally

inspections.text: The crate swings an inch and stops. “I. AM. WAITING. FOR. THE. WIND. STOP.”
inspections.title: Heron

inspections.text: It’s watching a valve wheel as if it might do something. “CHECKING. STILL CHECKING. STOP.”
inspections.title: Tender

inspections.text: “IT IS 9.14. LAMP TWO IS NOT DUE UNTIL 19.40. I AM EARLY. STOP.”
inspections.title: Wick

inspections.text: Planks stacked to dry, chalked with a guild mark and a date. A tarpaulin tied over the best of it.
inspections.title: Building timber

inspections.text: Initials cut into the seat: R.W. Varnished over more than once.
inspections.title: The garden bench

inspections.text: Somebody has left half a sandwich on the bench, neatly wrapped, as if they mean to come back.
inspections.title: A pocket park

inspections.text: Below the promenade, scattered trees and quiet yards lead down towards the harbour.
inspections.title: Over the rail

inspections.text: Down below, a man is carrying a ladder sideways along a street too narrow for it.
inspections.title: The east wall

inspections.text: Hill Street one way, the Harbour Steps the other. Someone has tied a ribbon round the Lantern Row arm, as if it might wander off.
inspections.title: The fingerpost

inspections.text: BAND TONIGHT, pasted over CIRCUS, pasted over a band from last summer. You can still make out the drummer’s name.
inspections.title: The poster column

inspections.text: The urn ticks as it cools. A cup sits upside down on its saucer, the way you leave one when you mean to come back.
inspections.title: The coffee cart

inspections.text: The way back up to the lane. Chalked on the bottom step: 212. Under it, in other chalk: LIAR. 213.
inspections.title: Spindle Steps

inspections.text: Jars in the window, every one labelled by hand. One label just says DON’T.
inspections.title: Thyme & Tonic

inspections.text: A slate by the opening: PLEASE DON’T PICK THE FOXGLOVE. Underneath, smaller: OR THE MINT.
inspections.title: The physic garden

terminals.locked: A brass-collared socket below the glass. Nell’s slate has the matching plug.
terminals.title: Square service screen
